claims.text: Flame spray pyrolysis can produce CeO2-ZrO2 supports with a high density of oxygen vacancies.
Depositing sub-monolayer Pt on oxygen-vacancy-rich CeO2-ZrO2 creates strong metal-support interactions.
Strong metal-support interactions stabilize ultra-small Pt clusters.
Strong metal-support interactions on oxygen-vacancy-rich CeO2-ZrO2 enhance oxygen activation.
The proposed catalyst will have greater catalytic activity than conventional Pt/Al2O3.
The proposed catalyst will have greater durability than conventional Pt/Al2O3.
The proposed catalyst will reduce overall Pt consumption.
Conventional catalysts typically use Pt supported on Al2O3 or CeO2-ZrO2.
Conventional supports have lower oxygen-vacancy concentrations than the proposed support.
Lower oxygen-vacancy concentrations result in less effective Pt dispersion and higher Pt loadings.
Oxygen vacancies physically and electronically stabilize highly dispersed Pt clusters.
Oxygen vacancies improve the oxygen-storage capacity of CeO2-ZrO2.
Oxygen vacancies facilitate strong metal-support interactions between Pt and CeO2-ZrO2.
The strong metal-support interaction promotes Pt redispersion.
The strong metal-support interaction prevents Pt agglomeration.
Improved Pt stabilization and oxygen activation allow equal or better catalytic performance with less Pt.
After accelerated aging under simulated exhaust conditions, the proposed catalyst will maintain higher pollutant-conversion rates than conventional Pt/Al2O3.
After accelerated aging under simulated exhaust conditions, the proposed catalyst will exhibit less Pt sintering than conventional Pt/Al2O3.
The proposed benefits should hold at 500–800 °C under lean-rich redox cycling in gas mixtures containing NOx and CO.
